title: Paloma and the Contact
premise: August Coldharbour, a gifted interpreter hiding a fabricated identity within a fractious peace delegation, receives a calendar invite from a handler who died three days ago—summoning them to a meeting that never should exist. Following the invitation pulls August into a conspiracy spanning three governments: a staged peace process designed to collapse on schedule, with the delegation as cover for an arms pipeline. Hunted by an assassin who knows their real name, August must decide whether to stay invisible or expose the truth with a ragtag found family of delegates, defectors, and one very dangerous informant. The truth gets out—but only because August finally surrenders the lie, standing in their own name as the assassin's bullet finds the wrong target.
about_author: Emrys Blackwood is a former conference interpreter who spent a decade in rooms where languages collided and truths got lost in translation. They write thrillers about people who survive by being someone else.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: August's POV. We meet August mid-interpretation at a fractious Geneva summit, fluent in four languages and fluent in one lie—their own identity. They keep a go-bag packed under the hotel bed. Emotional beat: controlled paranoia, the comfort of routines built to vanish.

chapters.title: Invitation from the Dead
chapters.summary: August's POV. A calendar ping: 'Meridian, tomorrow, 21:00'—from Handler Voss, confirmed dead in Vienna. August checks the obituary twice. The invitation includes a detail only Voss knew: the name August buried years ago. Emotional beat: dread curdling into compulsion—the past has a meeting time.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: August's POV. The meeting is a dead-drop with a voice recorder and a photograph: the peace treaty's annex is a laundering shell, and the delegation is scheduled to fail on a timeline. Voss recorded it before dying. Emotional beat: vertigo—August realizes invisibility was always someone else's design.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: August's POV. August maps who benefits: all three delegations have annex signatories. Telling any one government means trusting the conspiracy's own architects. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into resolve—no one is clean, so the truth needs an unusual courier.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Counts Ceilings
chapters.summary: Delegate Ilsa Reyes's POV. Ilsa, a burned-out auditor-turned-diplomat, notices the annex numbers don't reconcile—and notices August noticing. She corners August in a stairwell. Emotional beat: wary recognition between two people fluent in pretending.

chapters.title: A Man Named Nobody
chapters.summary: The assassin's POV. Codename Ferro arrives in Geneva with a file on 'August Coldharbour'—and a second, older file underneath it. He works methodically, politely. Emotional beat: cold professionalism laced with a hunter's genuine curiosity about his prey.

chapters.title: Translated Under Duress
chapters.summary: August's POV. A delegation security 'interview' about Voss's death becomes an interrogation; August's cover holds by a thread. They realize someone inside the delegation fed Ferro the guest list. Emotional beat: the lie that protected them now paints a target.

chapters.title: Found Family, Assembled Badly
chapters.summary: August's POV. August recruits Ilsa, plus Tam, a junior delegate's aide who can forge anything, and Dr. Okafor, a defector archivist hiding in plain sight. None trust each other. Emotional beat: awkward, necessary alliance—strangers choosing each other over safety.

chapters.title: The Vienna Precedent
chapters.summary: Dr. Okafor's POV. Okafor decrypts Voss's recorder: the annex scheme has a predecessor—a peace deal that 'failed' in Vienna five years ago, same signatures, same shell. Emotional beat: grief and vindication; the dead handler was telling the truth all along.

chapters.title: Safe House, Unsafe Company
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The group hides in Okafor's safe house; Ilsa and August trade half-truths over bad coffee until August admits the invitation was from a dead man. Ilsa stays anyway. Emotional beat: the first honest conversation—trust built on shared damage.

chapters.title: Ferro Closes Distance
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Ferro eliminates a courier chain and finds Okafor's archive trail. He sends August a message through a hotel TV: 'I know the name your mother gave you.' Emotional beat: the hunter's patience as horror—August's real identity is currency now.

chapters.title: The Deadline in the Annex
chapters.summary: August's POV. The recorder reveals the timeline: the delegation fails in nine days, the pipeline opens in ten. Going public means going through three intelligence services. Emotional beat: ticking-clock pressure fusing the group's purpose—no more options, only moves.

chapters.title: Tam's Beautiful Forgery
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam forges credentials to access the delegation's secure archive room; the plan nearly dies when a real archivist recognizes the badge format. Tam talks their way out with a forged friendship. Emotional beat: terror and pride—the least likely member saves the mission.

chapters.title: What Okafor Buried
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Inside the archive, Okafor finds the Vienna files—and her own name on a witness list she was supposed to die on. She confesses she's been running from these people longer than any of them knew. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into commitment; she stops fleeing.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Delegation
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The mole is exposed: the delegation's own security chief, feeding Ferro. A trap is sprung at the safe house; the group scatters, the recorder copies split between them. Emotional beat: betrayal's sting, and the choice to trust each other anyway—found family tested by fire.

chapters.title: The Name I Gave Away
chapters.summary: August's POV. Cornered, August finally tells Ilsa the truth: who they were before, why they buried it, why Voss's invitation used that name. Ferro listens from the next room. Emotional beat: the lie dies on August's own terms—identity reclaimed as weapon, not wound.

chapters.title: Ferro's File
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Ferro reviews his two files and realizes his employers lied to him about the target—the 'threat' is a witness to their crime. He hesitates for the first time in his career. Emotional beat: a killer's crisis of faith; the machine develops a conscience-shaped crack.

chapters.title: Nine Hours to Geneva
chapters.summary: August's POV. The group reconverges with a plan: broadcast the annex evidence during the treaty's closing plenary, using the interpretation booth—the one room where August's voice is authority. Emotional beat: desperate momentum; the invisible interpreter chooses to be heard.

chapters.title: The Booth
chapters.summary: August's POV. Climax. August goes off-script mid-interpretation, feeding the annex evidence into the live translation feed in three languages while Tam forces the documents onto every delegate's screen. Ferro breaches the building. Emotional beat: terrifying exposure—every word a confession and a weapon.

chapters.title: The Wrong Target
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Ferro has a clean shot at August as security storms the plenary. He fires—and hits the security chief, the real architect, arriving to silence August. Ferro walks out through the chaos, leaving his second file on August's desk. Emotional beat: ambiguous mercy; the assassin chooses his own justice.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Hearing
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Fallout: the treaty collapses, hearings begin, and the three governments scramble to disown the annex. Ilsa testifies; Tam and Okafor find new names for themselves—chosen ones, this time. Emotional beat: battered, imperfect vindication; justice outside the law, then slowly inside it.

chapters.title: August Coldharbour, Interpreter
chapters.summary: August's POV. Months later, August unpacks the go-bag at last and hangs a coat in a closet that isn't temporary. A new invitation arrives—from Ferro, just a set of coordinates and the word 'coffee.' August smiles, packs light, and goes. Emotional beat: peace chosen, not escaped; identity kept, family found, one door left deliberately open.
